Return all ICCs for the original variables.

Source: R/04_post_02_accessor_functions.R
get_ICC.Rd

You can use get_ICC() or get_ICCs() interchangeably.

Usage

get_ICC(object)

get_ICCs(object)

get_icc(object)

Arguments

object

A wbCorr object, created by the wbCorr() function.

Value

A dataframe with ICCs for all variables. The ICC(1,1) of the one-way random-effects model is estimated from ANOVA mean squares, using all available observations of each variable. Sample estimates can be negative.

See also

wbCorr

Examples

# importing our simulated example dataset with pre-specified within- and between- correlations
data("simdat_intensive_longitudinal")

# create object:
correlations <- wbCorr(data = simdat_intensive_longitudinal,
                      cluster = 'participantID')

# returns the ICCs:
ICCs <- get_ICC(correlations)
print(ICCs)
#>   variable         ICC
#> 1      day -0.02040816
#> 2     var1  0.51348244
#> 3     var2  0.49354674
#> 4     var3  0.49258895
